target: scripts/welcome.py, scripts/azoth-deploy.py, scripts/roadmap_dashboard.py, scripts/run_ledger.py, scripts/azoth-sync.py, scripts/do_closeout.py
summary: The 2026-04-23 performance automation measured a likely YAML-loader regression and recommends restoring a shared CSafeLoader-backed safe-load helper for hot scripts.
evidence: Automation thread 019db993-3769-7d53-badb-1d4310becddd measured `python3 scripts/welcome.py --plain` at mean 0.4730s versus prior automation memory baseline 0.1845s, and `python3 scripts/azoth-deploy.py --dry-run --platforms codex` at mean 0.1624s versus prior 0.0938s. The profile showed 0.455s cumulative in `yaml.safe_load`/PyYAML compose/construct under welcome.py, and microbenchmarks showed CSafeLoader reducing backlog parsing from ~176.78ms to ~10.95ms, roadmap from ~101.98ms to ~7.77ms, and patterns from ~36.08ms to ~1.37ms. The automation caveat is that the prior optimization was not visible in current git history, so the follow-up should re-measure before patching.
recommended_action: Open BL-071 as a scoped performance follow-up: confirm the regression on the active branch, add or restore a shared `scripts/yaml_helpers.py` safe-load wrapper using `yaml.CSafeLoader` when available, route hot scripts through it, and verify with focused tests plus before/after timings.
